# [CS051] Defer Inside a Loop (defer-in-loop)

defer is used in a loop body of the same function.

| | |
| --- | --- |
| **Severity** | MEDIUM |
| **Category** | Reliability & Concurrency |
| **CWE** | [CWE-400](https://cwe.mitre.org/data/definitions/400.html) |
| **OWASP** | A06:2025 |
| **Auto-Fix supported** | No |

## Why It Matters in Go

Deferred calls run when the function returns, not at the end of the iteration, so files, locks or rows acquired in each iteration stay open until the loop finishes. Move the body into a function literal or helper.

## Vulnerable / Problematic Example

```go
for _, p := range paths {
	f, err := os.Open(p)
	if err != nil {
		return err
	}
	defer f.Close()
	process(f)
}
```

## Safe / Idiomatic Go Pattern

```go
for _, p := range paths {
	if err := func() error {
		f, err := os.Open(p)
		if err != nil {
			return err
		}
		defer f.Close()
		return process(f)
	}(); err != nil {
		return err
	}
}
```

## Configuration & Suppression

Disable the rule for the whole module in `.codexsentinel.yaml`:

```yaml
rules:
  disabled: [defer-in-loop]
```

Change its severity:

```yaml
rules:
  severity_overrides:
    defer-in-loop: low
```

Suppress one reviewed finding on its line, with the reason:

```go
//codex:ignore defer-in-loop -- <reason>
```

Or ignore it under a path in `.codexsentinel.ignore`:

```text
internal/legacy/** defer-in-loop
```
